newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 20.

text.p: Wellington's Capital Coast Health has sent a young kidney patient home to die after deciding he is not capable of giving himself dialysis treatment. Peter Widdowson, 24, has been given two months to live after being discharged from Wellington Hospital's renal unit and told he does not qualify for the treatment that would keep him alive. Alliance health spokeswoman Phillida Bunkle said on Wednesday the policy leading to the decision was inhumane and indefensible. Page 1.

NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan has renounced his aspirations to chair the Maori Affairs select committee, saying he does not want his part in the Aotearoa Television Network saga to detract from its work "and cloud important Maori issues". Morgan is under fire for a lavish pre-election spendup on clothes using the struggling station's money after he had quit as a director. Page 1.

State Services commissioner Don Hunn said on Wednesday he "took seriously" admissions by Serious Fraud Office director Charles Sturt that he did not fully investigate the Winebox documents. Hunn said he would speak to Sturt about admissions he made at the Cook Islands tax commission of inquiry on Tuesday that he had made misleading statements about his inquiries. Page 1.

National is being urged to delay a referendum on compulsory superannuation to allow the completion of a review of the current voluntary system. The call was made by Labour and the Alliance at a meeting of superannuation accord parties on Wednesday afternoon, but NZ First leader Winston Peters later ruled out that option, saying there was too much work to be done in order to have the compulsory savings scheme ready for implementation by the deadline of July 1. Page 2.

Maori language broadcasting was dealt another blow on Wednesday with the closure of Aotearoa Maori Radio. The Auckland-based radio station has received more than $8 million in government funding since opening in June 1989. Its trustees blamed the Maori broadcasting funding agency Te Mangai Paho for their decision to close. Page 2.

ACT NZ branded opposition to a nuclear waste shipment through the Tasman Sea as "outdated hysteria" on Wednesday. The Pacific Teal, carrying radioactive waste from France to Japan, is due to pass through the Tasman soon. In Parliament on

Wednesday Alliance MP and Greens co-leader Jeannette Fitzsimons moved that Parliament declare that shipping radioactive waste through New Zealand's exclusive economic zone was prohibited under international law and agreements. Page 2.

Air New Zealand has kissed goodbye to the golden results of recent years, predicting tougher times as it battles a strong New Zealand dollar, higher fuel prices and fewer passengers on lucrative Asian routes. Natural Gas Corporation is expecting a better full-year profit than last year's $28 million, according to chief executive Richard Bentley. Natural Gas expects the "positive trading environment" to continue and the benefits of greater gas sales to ECNZ and Southdown power station will be seen in the second half of the financial year. Bentley would not give a figure for the expected full-year result. Page 11.

Heinz Wattie chief executive and area director David Irving, 50, is stepping down as chief executive to "move on to new opportunities", according to H J Heinz chairman Tony O'Reilly. The group expected to name a replacement for Irving shortly. Heinz Wattie is New Zealand's biggest grocery foods group. Page 11.

Corporate Investments' half-year profit was up seven percent to $11.07 million, but would have been more without higher interest rates. Interest expenses rose $710,000 to $10.42 million. However, the company said costs were expected to fall
$1.5 million for the second half-year. Group revenue rose eight percent for the period to $199.68 million. No dividend was declared. Page 11.

Carter Holt Harvey and CSR declined on Wednesday to comment on speculation that Carter Holt was poised to buy CSR's A$1 billion (NZ$1.10 billion) timber products business. The Sydney Morning Herald reported that Carter Holt could be close to a deal, saying the company had indicated a desire to expand its operations in Australia, particularly in medium-density fireboard. Page 11.
